methods.name: Compressed raw X6 integer dual bound and original equality fibers / 压缩 raw X6 整数对偶界与原始取等纤维
methods.description: Paper theorem composing positive-support raw compression with complete finite integer table potentials. It transfers a verified compressed-carrier linear bound to arbitrary finite original negative support and supplies the full gap and the precise equality-fiber conditions. 这是纸面条件定理，未实现通用对偶验证器。
triggers: compressed raw X6 integer dual certificate positive support finite carrier
X6 正支撑压缩 raw 有限整数对偶证书 原空间取等纤维
methods.input_contract: In one common external anchor and labelled raw integer X6 chart, aggregate two finite positive rational populations and Jordan-cancel first. Fix a nonempty positive support S with every w_s>0 and arbitrary finite negative population disjoint from S. Use the actual positive-support coordinate compression C=product_i(A_i union {max(A_i)+1}). Supply all twenty complete integer tables b_I:C_I->Z, integer L>0 and B>=0, with |b_I|<=L and F(z)=sum_I b_I(z_I)<=-B for every z in C minus S. The positive potentials a_s=F(s) may be signed and nonuniform.
methods.output_contract: The paper proves L*D>=sum_s(a_s*w_s)+B*N for every finite original negative population, with a full nonnegative table/negative-site gap. Equality requires all table gaps zero and original negative support inside phi^(-1)({F=-B}); a tight point has a singleton original fiber exactly when all its coordinates lie in their A_i. A uniform L*D>=A*M follows only with the additional positive A, all a_s>=A and B>=A conditions, with its own extra equality terms. The S-empty branch is D=20*N=20*M, and zero difference has no ratio.
methods.core_law: Raw compression preserves P,N and each of twenty marginal L1 norms because every positive projected address has a singleton fiber and other fibers combine only nonpositive mass. The finite table pairing proves the conditional linear bound and exact gap; pullback preserves the original raw semantics and exposes rather than erases non-singleton equality fibers.

result_scope.coordinate_carrier: A_i={s_i:s in S}; c_i=max(A_i)+1; C=product_i(A_i union {c_i})
result_scope.table_contract: all twenty complete b_I:C_I->Z; integer L>0; |b_I|<=L
result_scope.potential_contract: F=sum_I b_I; integer B>=0; F(z)<=-B for every z in C minus S
result_scope.positive_potentials: a_s=F(s); signed and nonuniform values allowed
result_scope.uniform_coefficient: native unevaluated DIV(L,A) only after A>0
result_scope.linear_equality_iff: all table-address gaps vanish and every actual negative compressed point has F=-B
result_scope.original_negative_support: subset phi^(-1)(Z), where Z={z in C minus S:F(z)=-B}
result_scope.singleton_fiber_iff: every coordinate of the compressed point belongs to its A_i
result_scope.uniform_equality_extra_conditions: all a_s=A; if N>0 also B=A, in addition to the linear equality conditions

methods.hard_boundary: RESULT_ONLY with no API and no new tool family. No generic dual verifier, optimal dual search, carrier enumeration or new arithmetic runtime is implemented here. Full verification of a supplied finite certificate would still be required; a few samples or a budget overrun do not prove or refute the theorem. B=0 and signed/nonuniform a_s remain linear bounds and do not automatically yield a positive uniform M coefficient. A tight-set support condition alone does not classify all equality weights; a failed all-Z singleton check does not preclude every possible further classification. This is not an all-p3 sharp theorem or closure of the parent research question. Signed analysis is not a negative native BRC primitive, and no microscopic/history recovery, formal Result, Working Truth or main admission is granted.

reuse_resolution.how_applied_or_why_not: The already reviewed paper composes positive-support compression, raw projection contracts and existing concrete star table-dual examples. This harvest exposes that conditional theorem and reuses the two already registered star IDs without copying their method objects. No mathematical implementation is executed.
